text.p: Shares in British drugs company Zeneca Group Plc tumbled on Friday after the company said it had been warned by the FDA of the United States after an inspection of one of its plants in northwest England.

A Zeneca spokesman said the company received a letter from the U.S. Food and Drugs Administration saying it would not recommend approval of any new applications listing Zeneca as the manufacturer of sterile pharmaceuticals until reinspections have been carried out and corrections undertaken.
Zeneca shares fell 38.5 pence to 18 pounds in response to the news.

The spokesman said the company was fully committed to resolving the matter and had met with FDA officials. "We are confident of resolving the issue, and we are continuing to supply out of Macclesfield," the spokesman said.
